visual_action: Close-up of the propeller hub (cross bore visible), camera pulls back to a three-quarter view of the real assembled fan; crank turning, propeller following; title, subtitle, identity line
narration: A hand-cranked, gear-driven handheld fan: no motor, no battery, every part 3D printed.
technical_information: Geometry: fan_A.1.igs. Hand-cranked, gear-driven, no motor, no battery

visual_action: Chapter card; orbit of the assembled CAD model with B-rep edges; overall dimensions
narration: Stage one: the CAD model, the team's own assembly.
technical_information: Body 125 x 70 x 34 mm (measured from the IGES)

visual_action: Staggered explode along the shaft axis (X); README component labels with leaders; cap flagged as reconstructed
narration: Exploded along its shafts: two shell halves, a crank, three gears, two shafts, three axle pins, a propeller.
technical_information: 12 IGES bodies + reconstructed cap; 3 axle pins; compound gear not listed in README

visual_action: Collapse with shells in x-ray; crank, 54T gear, compound 12T/54T and 12T pinion highlighted in turn; rotation arrows; mesh points
narration: The crank's fifty-four-tooth gear drives a twelve-tooth pinion on a compound gear, whose large gear drives the propeller's pinion.
technical_information: Tooth counts measured: 54/12 and 54/12, module 1 mm

visual_action: Gear train turning (slowed); propeller blur; speed-up panel
narration: Two speed-up stages: in theory, about twenty propeller turns per crank turn.
technical_information: i = (54/12)^2 = 20.25 : 1, theoretical; compound turns opposite, propeller same direction as crank

visual_action: Shaft axes through both shells, 33.0 mm centre-distance dimensions; 'what CAD lets you check' panel
narration: CAD is where fit, alignment, centre distance and clearance are checked, before printing.
technical_information: Centre distance 33.0 mm = m(z1+z2)/2; blade-to-face clearance 6.7 mm; stepped rim joint

visual_action: Chapter card + question; the 12 bodies lay out as separate files with real triangle counts
narration: Stage two: STL export. Each part gets its own file, as each is printed separately.
technical_information: One STL per printed part (12 files exported from the IGES)

visual_action: Compound gear: sweep from exact CAD surface to faceted triangle mesh (coarse for visibility)
narration: The exact CAD surfaces become a mesh of flat triangles.
technical_information: Coarse 1,520 triangles shown; exported file 5,612 triangles at 0.01 mm deviation

visual_action: Outward normals, OD dimension, checks panel; gear rotates 54T face down with build-direction arrow
narration: The mesh is checked: closed, normals outward, scale in millimetres; then oriented for printing.
technical_information: Checks verified on this export: watertight, outward normals, mm scale (OD 56.0)

visual_action: Chapter card + question; all parts drop onto two 220 x 220 mm plates in the report's orientations; orientation labels
narration: Stage three: slicing. Parts lie flat on the plate: shells open side up, gears flat, so each tooth forms within every layer.
technical_information: Report 5.1 orientations; all parts fit 220 x 220 beds

visual_action: Slice plane rises; CAD above the plane, coloured toolpaths below; legend; close-up of one compound-gear layer
narration: The slicer cuts each part into thin layers and plans every toolpath: walls, then infill.
technical_information: Walls, inner walls, sparse infill, solid skin, brim, support from the real cross-sections

visual_action: Assumed starting-values panel; housing plate with the back-shell support callout
narration: The report suggests finer layers and extra walls for gears; supports go only where an overhang needs them.
technical_information: Report 5.2 values labelled assumed; back shell's outer bosses stand 2 mm proud, so its face needs support

visual_action: Chapter card; representative printer; hot-end cross-section schematic with moving filament and melt zone
narration: Stage four: FDM printing. Filament is melted in a heated nozzle and laid along the planned path.
technical_information: Printer and filament not specified in the project; 0.4 mm nozzle / PLA are report assumptions

visual_action: First layer of the compound gear: outer wall, inner walls, skin; planned-path inset synced to the nozzle; nozzle +0.16 mm
narration: The first layer bonds to the bed; the nozzle then rises one layer, and each layer fuses to the last.
technical_information: 81 layers at 0.16 mm (assumed); fresh road shown hot behind the nozzle

visual_action: Time-lapse: 54T gear then 12T pinion grow layer by layer; layer counter
narration: Nothing is cut away: the gear is built up, teeth first, then its pinion.
technical_information: Additive: material only where the part is

visual_action: Front shell walls rising (time-lapse)
narration: Shell walls grow the same way, leaving fine layer lines.
technical_information: 0.20 mm layers (assumed); layer lines

visual_action: Print complete, bed cooling indicator, all 12 printed parts on two plates, parts lifted off
narration: When the print ends, the bed cools before parts are removed.
technical_information: Remove parts after the bed cools (report 5)

visual_action: Chapter card + question; printed parts on the bench (layer-line material)
narration: Stage five: finishing. A printed part is not yet a mechanism.
technical_information: Illustrative sequence; report 5.3

visual_action: Hobby knife trims the propeller brim and strings; sanding the gear flanks, flank-profile inset (illustrative)
narration: Brims and strings are trimmed; gear flanks and shafts are sanded to remove layer ridges.
technical_information: 400-800 grit (report)

visual_action: Reaming a boss hole with a drill bit in a pin vise; lubricant drop on the teeth
narration: Pin holes are reamed so shafts turn freely, and the gears are lubricated.
technical_information: Ream to pin size; silicone grease or machine oil (report)

visual_action: Propeller spun three times on its shaft between supports, stopping at different angles; dial panel
narration: Balanced on its shaft, the propeller should stop at random angles.
technical_information: Balanced rotor stops at random angles (report)

visual_action: Chapter card; in bench orientation: pins, 54T gear + crank shaft, compound gear, pinion, top pin drop into the front shell; turn by hand
narration: Stage six: assembly and test. The crank gear, compound gear and propeller pinion go into the shell, meshing.
technical_information: Report 6 order, extended for the compound gear found in the CAD

visual_action: Back shell closes; crank handle, propeller shaft, propeller and cap fitted from outside; fan stands upright
narration: The second shell closes the train; the crank handle, propeller and cap go on last.
technical_information: No screws, clips or electronics

visual_action: Crank turning, back shell in x-ray showing both stages, propeller blur, airflow direction arrows; 'by design' panel
narration: By design, the crank drives both gear stages, so the propeller spins far faster than the hand.
technical_information: Theoretical 20.25 : 1, same direction as crank

visual_action: Test-plan table: test, method, pass criterion, result 'to be measured'
narration: The test plan: fit, free rotation, speed ratio, airflow, endurance and balance. Results are still to be measured.
technical_information: Report 7.1: no measured results exist

visual_action: Assembled CAD model orbit to a three-quarter view; six-stage chain; closing statement; gentle fade
narration: From CAD model to finished product: one digital design, six stages, no tooling.
technical_information: CAD -> STL -> Slicing -> FDM Printing -> Finishing -> Assembly & Test
